title: Palm Oil Mill-to-Port Traceability
thesis: Every CPO tank truck that leaves a fictional Malaysian mill for a port bulking terminal is a custody transfer. Snowflake turns those transfers into traceability-to-plantation and flag-precision KPIs, a 7-day custody-break risk score per mill, mass-balance variance anomalies and grounded AI answers, all on curated dynamic tables.

talking_points: Start with the question a bulking terminal buyer asks: how much of the CPO we received can be traced to a plantation? 40 mills across 8 Malaysian towns in Sabah, Sarawak and Peninsular Malaysia, 5 sourcing models.
Every KPI is a numerator over a denominator in a curated dynamic table, so it can be traced back to mill-day rows.
The custody-signal chart shows which checks lead to confirmed custody breaks and which mostly produce false-positive flags.
show: Daily CPO custody transfers and custody flags
tabs.call_out: One governed definition of traceable CPO, from mill gate to port

transition.line: Which mills should the traceability team visit first?

talking_points: Snowflake ML classification ranks mills by the probability of a confirmed custody break in the next 7 days, so audits go where they matter.
The holdout line shows precision and recall on the most recent labelled days, against the base rate.
Anomaly detection flags mass-balance variance outliers per mill, and the forecast projects network-wide CPO custody transfers for 14 days.
tabs.call_out: Honest, evaluated ML inside the data platform

transition.line: Is the supplier registry keeping up?

talking_points: Mass-balance reconciliation rate, FFB supplier link coverage and supplier verifications still pending.
The scatter compares each mill's reconciliation rate with its confirmed custody breaks.
tabs.call_out: Close supplier-link gaps before the bulking terminal buyer asks for plantation evidence

transition.line: What happens when a transfer arrives out of tolerance?

talking_points: CPO custody-transfer events land in RAW.LIVE_TRANSFERS: simulated in Snowflake, or from Amazon Data Firehose through S3 and Snowpipe in the AWS build.
FLAG events (a transfer whose mass-balance variance is out of tolerance) are logged by the alert, which emails the team.
tabs.call_out: From mill weighbridge to custody alert in one platform

talking_points: The Cortex Agent answers with generated SQL over the semantic view and cites the synthetic chain-of-custody SOPs by ID.
The action memo is drafted only from KPI, mill, custody-signal and risk rows; custody checks are demo signals, not audit or certification verdicts.
show: Agent answer with SQL and SOP citations
tabs.call_out: Answers carry their SQL and SOP IDs, so nobody has to trust a number blindly

transition.line: Here is how it is built.

talking_points: Both builds share the same core: seeded data, dynamic tables, Snowflake ML, Cortex Search, semantic view, agent, alert and task graph.
The AWS build adds Amazon Data Firehose, S3 and Snowpipe ingestion, a Bedrock memo and a QuickSight dashboard with an Amazon Q topic.
